chunks: What al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd narrated from Ḥammād ibn ʿĪsā, from Shuʿayb, from Abū Baṣīr, who said:

I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about supererogatory prayer in the night and the day. He said: What is recommended not to be reduced from it is eight rakʿahs at the sun’s decline, two rakʿahs after ẓuhr, two rakʿahs before ʿaṣr, two rakʿahs after maghrib, two rakʿahs before al-ʿatamah, and in the pre-dawn time eight rakʿahs; then he performs witr, and the witr is three separate rakʿahs; then two rakʿahs before salat al-fajr. And the most beloved time of salat al-layl to them is the latter part of the night.
So it is clarified in this report that these forty-six rakʿahs are among what is recommended not to fall short of, and that what is besides them does not share with them in this recommendation.

As for the reports other than these two reports that imply a reduction from fifty rakʿahs, their basis in all of them is Zurārah, even if they are repeated with different chains. We have fully covered what relates to this chapter in Kitāb Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām and clarified the aspect of it there, so whoever wishes to examine all of them should refer to it.

key_terms.زَوَالِ: the sun’s decline from its zenith, marking the time around noon
key_terms.مَفْصُولَةً: performed separately, with the rakʿahs distinguished from one another
key_terms.يُسْتَحَبُّ: recommended in law and encouraged to be observed
key_terms.ٱلتَّطَوُّعِ: supererogatory prayer performed voluntarily beyond the obligatory salat
key_terms.ٱلسَّحَرِ: the pre-dawn portion of the night
key_terms.ٱلِٱسْتِحْبَابِ: the quality of being recommended in sacred law
key_terms.ٱلْعَتَمَةِ: the night prayer time, referring to ʿishāʾ
key_terms.ٱلْوَتْرُ: the concluding odd-numbered prayer of the night prayer sequence

ai.seo_question: What are the recommended nafilah rakʿahs in the day and night according to Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This report outlines the recommended daily and nightly supererogatory prayers and identifies a set of forty-six rakʿahs that should not ordinarily be reduced. It also notes that the latter part of the night is the most beloved time for salat al-layl and refers readers to a fuller treatment of variant reports in Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām.
